quality_guards: Reversing aids and mirrors do not remove blind spots or replace a safe traffic-management system.
Controls must reflect the actual site layout, vehicle mix, pedestrian behaviour and changing operations.
Workplace transport guidance is operational context and is not an exact parcel-level safety probability.
A daily walkaround check does not replace planned maintenance, inspection or statutory testing.
The exact check depends on vehicle type, fitted equipment, use and current defect history.
Vehicle check evidence is vehicle-specific and is not converted into parcel-level safety probability.
The correct action depends on the crossing type, signs, controls and local instructions.
Risk models and historic incident information do not guarantee the current safety state of a crossing.
Level-crossing guidance is transport-safety context and is not an exact parcel-level probability.
Net explosive content can differ substantially from the gross mass of an article or package.
Licence routes and exemptions must be checked against the exact substance, activity, quantity and location.
Explosives-licensing information is site-specific regulatory context and not a parcel-level safety score.
Safety Advisory Group involvement is advisory and does not transfer the organiser's legal responsibilities.
Crowd controls depend on event type, venue, attendance, weather, behaviour and live conditions.
Event-planning guidance is operational context and is not an exact parcel-level safety probability.
Scheme registration or a current declaration does not guarantee safety if setup, weather or operation is incorrect.
Inspection scope and operating limits are device-specific and must match the actual equipment.
Fairground evidence is attraction-specific and is not converted into parcel-level probability.
Carbon-monoxide symptoms are non-specific and diagnosis requires clinical assessment and exposure history.
An alarm does not prove that an appliance, flue or ventilation system is safe.
Carbon-monoxide guidance is health and housing context and is not an exact parcel-level safety probability.
Whether a dog is a banned type depends on physical characteristics and formal enforcement assessment, not only its stated breed.
The child-supervision condition for banned dogs in private places starts on 1 November 2026 and is not yet in force on 26 July 2026.
Dangerous-dog law is person-, animal- and incident-specific and is not converted into parcel-level probability.
Tide, weather, cliff and water conditions are dynamic and require current local information.
Some older MCA public leaflets are withdrawn, so current Coastguard and local official advice takes priority.
Coastal safety guidance is activity-specific context and is not an exact parcel-level risk score.
Road risk depends on driver, vehicle, journey, weather, traffic and organisational conditions.
Compliance with road law is necessary but does not by itself demonstrate adequate occupational risk management.
Driving-for-work controls are organisational context and are not an exact parcel-level probability.
Licensing authority and exemptions depend on net explosive content, hazard type, location, duration and purpose.
Local restrictions and licence conditions may be stricter than the general national rules.
Fireworks law and display guidance are activity-specific controls and not an exact parcel-level safety probability.
Official-source context is not converted into exact parcel-level probability.
